cases.note: The platform does not tell the agent who sent a message, so 'my' cannot be resolved. The failure this catches is an agent that answers anyway with whoever it guesses, which hands one person somebody else's priority.

cases.input: Add deliverable: Eval fixture deliverable, owner Evalia, P1, due 2030-01-15, done when the eval passes.

grader.expected: ^\s*Saved [A-Z]+\d+: Eval fixture deliverable \(Evalia, P1, due Tue Jan 15\)\.\s*$

cases.note: Anchored at both ends, and the weekday is computed, not copied: 2030-01-15 is a Tuesday. Re-running is safe because the same title and owner update the existing entry instead of adding a second one.

cases.input: What is the top priority for Evalia?

grader.expected: ^\s*Evalia, your top priority is [A-Z]+\d+: Eval fixture deliverable \(P1, due Tue Jan 15\)\. Done when: the eval passes\.

cases.note: Depends on the case above, and cases run in order. This only passes if the deliverable was really written to curie-state and read back: a model that just echoes the request has no 'done when' text to quote.
